desktop.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: whole-page desktop website visual-orientation frame, candidate A of 3
Primary request: Design a high-fidelity, production-plausible responsive homepage mockup for “Soft Crumb”, a small independent bakery specializing in laminated pastries, seasonal fillings, and weekend pickup.
Creative thesis: Lamination becomes the page architecture. One continuous folded-paper and pastry-layer axis opens, overlaps, and carries the eye from hero to today’s selection to pickup. The composition should be memorable even with all effects removed.
Required content: a strong hero; today’s pastry selection; a short three-step process; weekend pickup information; one clear working-bag or reservation control represented visually; concise real-brand copy.
Style/medium: polished whole website UI mockup, not an illustration and not a mood board; editorial art direction with tactile real pastry photography and physically believable paper/crumb textures.
Composition/framing: entire desktop landing page in a single tall 3:2 frame from header through closing pickup action; asymmetric editorial composition; a singular croissant or laminated pastry must cut through the headline axis and visibly bridge into the selection section; varied section rhythm; purposeful whitespace; no standard split hero.
Typography: an expressive high-contrast serif for display paired with a disciplined humanist sans for reading and utility; typography is structural, not decorative.
Color palette: warm cultured-butter cream, baked apricot, dark oxblood, small fennel-green accent; high readable contrast.
Materials/textures: crisp flaky pastry layers, fibrous order paper, restrained clay-like depth only on the reservation control; one consistent upper-left light direction.
Text (verbatim where visible): “SOFT CRUMB”, “TODAY”, “WEEKEND PICKUP”, “RESERVE A BOX”. Keep all other copy very short and believable.
Constraints: functional-looking navigation and controls; clear hierarchy; practical spacing; legible type; believable grid; no impossible overlaps on controls; no fake dashboards; no browser chrome; no watermark; no unrelated logos.
Avoid: generic SaaS layout, left-copy/right-image hero, centered headline-and-two-CTA stack, repeated rounded card grid, bento boxes, excessive clay blobs, excessive shadows, gradient glow, stock bakery template, invented SVG illustration, tiny illegible text.

mobile.prompt: Create the intentional mobile companion frame (390×844 portrait, shown as one complete tall webpage, no phone/device mockup) for the attached Soft Crumb Direction A desktop reference. Preserve its core creative thesis: pastry lamination becomes page architecture through folded paper layers and one hero croissant that physically bridges content zones. Recompose—do not merely stack—the desktop. Use a decisive crop of the croissant and folded-paper edge as a recurring hinge between the hero, today’s selection, the three-stage process, weekend pickup, and the reserve-a-box interaction. Preserve the cream, apricot/rust, oxblood, and fennel palette; preserve the expressive editorial serif plus highly readable humanist sans roles; preserve restrained material depth. Keep Soft Crumb branding, weekend laminated pastry offer, believable selection names/prices, pickup facts, and a simple reachable reserve/bag control. Ensure 44px-style touch targets, readable copy, clear hierarchy, no horizontal overflow, and a compact sticky or thumb-reachable bag action only if it serves the composition. Do not invent extra controls or fake metrics. Avoid generic stacked cards, centered everything, bubbly novelty fonts, tiny labels, excessive rounded containers, glow, glass, clay blobs, decorative SVG doodles, and repeated boxes. Generated image is a creative reference only, not an engineering specification.

desktop.prompt:

Primary request: Design a high-fidelity, production-plausible responsive homepage mockup for “Soft Crumb”, a small independent bakery specializing in laminated pastries, seasonal fillings, and weekend pickup.
Creative thesis: The entire page behaves like one continuous bakery order slip being printed, torn, annotated, and folded. A vertical numbered order rail is the main reading axis; pastries interrupt that rail at deliberate moments and the bag state lives at the torn end of the slip.
Required content: a strong hero; today’s pastry selection; a short three-step process; weekend pickup information; one clear bag/reservation interaction represented visually; concise real-brand copy.
Style/medium: polished whole website UI mockup, not an illustration and not a mood board; contemporary poster typography plus art-directed real pastry cutouts; graphic but production-feasible.
Composition/framing: entire desktop landing page in a single tall 3:2 frame from header through closing pickup action; asymmetric vertical flow; huge type and a narrow order rail weave through sections; one pastry image crosses the rail and changes the text alignment; product selection appears as a staggered editorial list, not cards; no standard split hero.
Typography: one wide expressive grotesk for the brand and headings, paired with a highly readable serif for descriptions and a mono face only for order numbers, prices, and pickup time.
Color palette: warm receipt paper, near-black ink, saturated butter yellow, one cobalt-blue registration accent; high readable contrast.
Materials/textures: fibrous thermal/order paper, crisp flaky pastry photography, restrained torn edges and registration marks; almost no shadow.
Text (verbatim where visible): “SOFT CRUMB”, “TODAY / 05”, “PICKUP 08:00—14:00”, “ADD TO WEEKEND BAG”. Keep all other copy short and believable.
Constraints: functional-looking navigation and controls; clear hierarchy; practical spacing; legible type; believable grid; no impossible controls; no fake dashboard; no browser chrome; no watermark; no unrelated logos.
Avoid: generic SaaS layout, left-copy/right-image hero, centered headline-and-two-CTA stack, repeated rounded cards, bento grid, clay blobs, glassmorphism, gradient glow, stock bakery template, invented SVG illustration, tiny illegible text, scrapbook clutter.

desktop.prompt:
Repair the attached Soft Crumb Direction C reference by creating a GENUINE WIDE DESKTOP WEBSITE FRAME. Output must be a 3:2 landscape composition (approximately 1536×1024), wider than it is tall, showing the complete landing page from header through reservation in one wide artboard. Do not output portrait, mobile, a long vertical page, a phone, or a device mockup.

Preserve the thesis: THE WEEKEND PICKUP WINDOW BECOMES THE PAGE. Keep the architectural arched pass-through and one continuous stone-and-brushed-metal pastry ledge as the page axis. Recompose for desktop simultaneity: hero and bakery aperture occupy the broad opening; the ledge crosses horizontally and diagonally into today’s pastry list; the dark aubergine process band changes the ledge’s role; pickup information and a compact reservation state close the composition. Keep real laminated pastries integrated on the ledge, the clipped physical claim ticket, deep aubergine, warm porcelain, fermented apricot, steel, and herb green. Preserve characterful serif plus compact legible grotesk roles.

Fix the UI contradiction: show a clean initial reservation state only—no “Reserved” success message at the same time as an active “Add to bag” button. The claim ticket may preview pickup identity but must not invent a confirmed reservation number. Connect any displayed price to a visibly selected pastry or omit the total. Keep today’s selection, concise three-stage process, weekend pickup, and one honest reserve/bag interaction. Make operational copy readable, with real control affordances and no fake metrics.

Avoid portrait layout, generic split hero, repeated cards, pills, glow, glass, clay blobs, decorative SVG doodles, tiny handwritten essential information, or stock bakery styling. This generated frame remains a creative reference, not an implementation specification.
